correctness.rationale: For the sign convention exp(+εI), the uniform centered Mallows score is Z=I−E[I]; the PL score is S_i=1−H_n+H_{n−R_i}. The first-choice term is strictly convex on centered log-weights, all later terms are convex, and positive target mass on rankings beginning with a minimum-weight item gives a cross-entropy lower bound proportional to the log-weight range. Hence the minimizer exists and is unique on the centered subspace; the positive Hessian and implicit function theorem give its local expansion. The quadratic KL term is E[(εZ−θ·S)^2]/2 by a Taylor expansion of normalized smooth families (PL need not be treated as a joint exponential family). Uniform selection-stage martingale increments give G_ii=(n−H_n)/n, and the centered eigenvalue is (n−H_n)/(n−1). Conditioning Z on a label's rank and summing against S_i gives b_i=(i−(n+1)/2)/2; the inversion variance then yields the stated coefficient and derivative. At n=2 the families coincide. At n≥3, swapping the same two labels at two different adjacent ranks changes the inversion score by one but a linear combination of PL scores by a label difference divided by two different stage sizes, proving the residual is positive. The harmonic asymptotic gives n³/288 for the coefficient, not a uniform ε expansion.
residual_risks: Bounded replay covers all permutations for 2≤n≤6, checking score centering, full score covariance, cross-covariance, inversion variance and projection; it gives C_3=5/168. It is not an asymptotic proof. Separate optimizer experiments mentioned in the frozen record were not relied upon; no Lean or expert attestation claimed.

evidence: Turvey excludes Mallows q≠1 at n≥4 from the larger class obtained by ranking independent continuous variables, which contains PL. The 2018 study discusses both model families and empirical KL in noisy-sorting experiments.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Non-representability for the larger class is stronger as an exclusion, but does not quantify even the order of vanishing of the distance to the PL model, evaluate the derivative of the PL minimizer, or treat the n=3 case at issue. Empirical model fit is not an analytic KL projection formula.

value.rationale: The result quantifies the error and gives the optimal first-order calibration when replacing a Mallows law with the computationally convenient item-weight family near uniformity. In particular it detects positive quadratic loss already at three items, below the range of the cited broader non-representability theorem, and gives a usable scale as n grows. It does more than establish that the families differ or report finite fit experiments.
residual_risks: Fixed-n local expansion, one direction of KL only; no accuracy asserted for a joint growth limit or for parameters away from uniformity.
